12b8745ffd.q: How does Parasoft's test impact analysis technology help scale AI-generated code testing?
12b8745ffd.a: Test impact analysis is a dedicated technology that for every single build from development teams, identifies exactly which tests were impacted by code changes. It tells you the exact subset of tests you need to rerun which will touch every single line of modified code, allowing you to validate applications generated by AI without running all tests every time.

66c7c49ece.q: What is the risk of relying completely on AI to test applications without creating persistent tests?
66c7c49ece.a: Complete reliance on AI to self-discover application capabilities and test everything creates visibility problems. You lose repeatability of test results because if you make code refactoring changes, you cannot confirm that previous behavior was not broken since the AI rediscovers capabilities each time, and you have no persistent record of what was actually tested.

4c67a3d9f4.q: Why is code coverage still essential for software quality even when using AI-generated code and tests?
4c67a3d9f4.a: Absence of execution of code keeps you up at night because unexecuted code will break in the real world—that's Murphy's Law. If your code coverage is only 60%, you cannot sleep at night. But if at least 100% of the code has been executed with meaningful tests, you probably can sleep at night knowing there is no unknown risk in deployment.

f5f3376aa8.q: How do traditional testing methodologies fail when testing non-deterministic AI-powered applications?
f5f3376aa8.a: Traditional testing assumes you send requests and get the same response every time, which you can validate consistently. With non-deterministic applications where AI is part of the system, responses could be different but still correct—appearing in different forms and shapes. Your traditional test methodology starts failing because you cannot assert on something that continues to change.

50a539d766.q: What is the difference between using AI to generate tests once versus using AI to maintain deterministic tests continuously?
50a539d766.a: One approach uses AI to create tests and then throws them away—treating testing like a room of super monkeys performing rough testing on the fly, where you pay more for more monkeys. A better scalable approach uses conventional test creation methods where tests are executed repeatedly, run deterministically, and when tests fail, you understand exactly which tests failed and why, making the tests themselves an asset rather than disposable.
